text:
ravi: Quick report - Go GeneratorStream Recv() isn't returning immediately on ctx cancel. JS/Python cancel fast, Go sleeps ~150ms.

claire: Does your SDK call http.NewRequestWithContext? If not, cancel won't interrupt reads reliably (esp http2).

ravi: We're using client.Do(req) where req was created without ctx. Minimal repro attached.

owen: Two fixes: (1) make GeneratorStream use NewRequestWithContext(ctx,...); (2) expose stream.Abort() that closes resp.Body. Abort is simple immediate mitigation.

ravi: Agree. Also saw auth-refresh code that rebuilt requests without the caller ctx - that's a regression for cancel propagation.

claire: I'll PR: use req = http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, ...) and add stream.Abort() that calls resp.Body.Close(). Add integration test: fake runtime writes two chunks 200ms apart, cancel after first, expect context.Canceled within 50ms.

owen: Add docs note in onboarding sampleapp: defer stream.Abort()/Close() after getting stream.

qa-bot: Created ticket #701: go-sdk: ensure streaming cancel parity and add stream.Abort() (assigned to @claire).

ravi: Thanks! Will update sampleapp once PR lands.
